title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from p.45). Grothendieck has made a 'nouveau départ' for an axiomatic combinatorial 'analysis situs'. A 'contrée' C is a triple (M, F, Σ):
- M is a set of 'multistructures', thought of as cells or simplices.
- F ⊂ P(M) is a family of subsets called figures.
- Σ is a relation 'F' is a subdivision of F' on figures.
Axiom C1: every X ∈ M lies in a smallest figure F_X, the elementary figure of X. Axiom C'1: F_X ≠ F_Y whenever X ≠ Y. One sets X ≤ Y iff F_X ⊂ F_Y (equivalently X ∈ F_Y). This is an order relation, not just a preorder, thanks to C'1.

This page.
(1) Figures are lower sets. If F is a figure and X ∈ F, then F_X ⊂ F by minimality. So Y ≤ X (Y ∈ F_X) gives F_Y ⊂ F_X ⊂ F, hence Y ∈ F. Thus every figure is a ≤-closed (downward closed) subset of M, and F_X is the principal ideal ↓X. The diagonal, partly struck-out margin note seems to say that M is thereby identified with the set of elementary figures F_X ordered by inclusion.
(2) Compatibility. Two figures F, G are compatible if F ∪ G is a figure. Two elements X, Y are compatible if F_X and F_Y are.
(3) Axiom C2: F and G are compatible iff every X ∈ F and Y ∈ G are compatible. A struck-out corollary apparently characterised compatible pairs X, Y as those lying in a common figure.
(4) Axiom C3 (sub-figures): a subset of a figure F is a figure iff it is ≤-closed.
(5) The empty figure. If M ≠ ∅, C3 applied to any F_X makes ∅ a figure. If M = ∅ one must decide whether F = ∅ or F = {∅*}; Grothendieck stipulates the latter, so the empty figure always exists. A margin note says 'cas trivial si M = ∅'.
(6) A margin arrow labelled 'intersection' points at C2/C3. Intersections of two figures are lower subsets of a figure, so they are figures by C3.

Purpose. This is the incidence-combinatorial skeleton of a 'tame' polyhedral topology. Figures behave like subcomplexes of a cell or simplicial complex: closed under faces, glued along pairwise compatibility. The next page uses this skeleton to define refinement (F ≪ G iff G is a sub-figure of a subdivision of F). Axiom C4 there ensures that subdivisions of sub-figures extend, so that refinement is an order.

Structural consequence (implicit, not stated on the page). Compatibility is reflexive and symmetric. It is inherited downward: F_{X'} ∪ F_Y ⊂ F_X ∪ F_Y is a lower set, hence a figure by C3. By induction with C2, a finite lower set is a figure iff its elements are pairwise compatible. So, for finitely generated figures, (M, ≤, non-compatibility) has exactly the axioms of a prime event structure (partial order, symmetric irreflexive conflict inherited upward), and figures are its configurations. One can equally read it as a 'flag' condition: a figure is a downward-closed clique of the compatibility graph.
errors: No real errors. Necessity in C2 is not independent: it already follows from C3, since F_X ∪ F_Y is a lower subset of the figure F ∪ G. Only the 'suffit' direction is a genuine axiom.
The empty-figure discussion is slightly muddled in the manuscript, with struck-out 'cela signifie que'. The point is that ∅ ∈ F follows from C1+C3 when M ≠ ∅ and must be postulated when M = ∅.

Infinite figures are not controlled. C2 handles only unions of two figures, so an arbitrary pairwise-compatible lower set need not be a figure without a further (finiteness or directed-union) axiom. Presumably M is implicitly locally finite.

ideas.what: Axiomatization of a 'contrée' as a set of cells with a family of 'figures' (subcomplexes) and a subdivision relation; elements ordered by inclusion of their elementary (closure) figures
ideas.modern_name: Abstract cell/simplicial complex as a face poset with subcomplexes = lower sets; closure operator / Alexandrov topology on a poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical combinatorial topology (Poincaré, Tucker, Alexandrov); face posets of regular CW complexes (Björner, 1980s)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (§5–6); the 'contrée' axiomatics appear unpublished

ideas.what: Compatibility of figures (union is a figure) and axiom C2: compatibility of figures is pairwise compatibility of elements
ideas.modern_name: Binary conflict relation / flag (clique) condition; prime event structure configurations; coherence-space-like binary coherence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nielsen–Plotkin–Winskel (event structures, 1981); Girard (coherence spaces, 1987); flag complexes (Gromov)

ideas.what: Axiom C3: lower subsets of a figure are figures (sub-figures); intersections of figures are figures; empty figure
ideas.modern_name: Subcomplex closure (hereditary family of lower sets)

missed.claim: Axioms C1, C'1, C2 and C3 make (M, ≤, incompatibility) a prime event structure, with finite figures exactly its configurations. Equivalently, figures are downward-closed cliques of a 'coherence' relation. Grothendieck's combinatorial foundation for tame topology thus coincides formally with the event-structure / coherence-space formalism from concurrency and linear logic, developed independently around the same time (1981–87). No one seems to have related his 'contrées' to those structures.
missed.quote: Pour que F et G soient compatibles, il faut et suffit que ∀X∈F, Y∈G, X et Y le soient.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Directed/concurrent topology and the geometric semantics of concurrency (Goubault, Fajstrup, Raussen) use cubical/simplicial models of event structures. Grothendieck's subdivision axioms (C4 on the next page) could supply a refinement theory for such models, and conversely. The link is formal and modest.

missed.claim: The 'contrée' axiomatics, a purely combinatorial poset-plus-subdivision foundation for analysis situs/tame topology, is begun but its development is unpublished. Infinite figures are not controlled by the axioms stated here.
missed.quote: Une contrée C est définie par un triple (M, F, Σ)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a documented attempt at the 'topologie modérée' of Esquisse d'un programme. Historians and those working on combinatorial models of tame topology (o-minimal triangulation, PL subdivision posets) may find this a primary source.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on this page is elementary order-theoretic bookkeeping. Its interest lies in being part of an unpublished foundational attempt at tame topology, and in a formal, probably unnoticed, coincidence with event structures and coherence spaces.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 likely reads 'Si F est une figure, alors X ∈ F ⇔ F_X ⊂ F' (':' / '⇒' in the transcription). The struck-out heading above F_X appears to be a scratched word ('élément'?).
The struck-out corollary probably reads 'pour que X, Y ∈ M soient compatibles, il faut et il suffit qu'ils appartiennent à une même figure'.
The left-margin note near C2 reads roughly 'cf./comment. : Fig 9', with a separate note 'intersection' and an arrow pointing from C2 to C3.

At the bottom, 'on suppose que c'est le deuxième cas' is probably 'on suppose que [dans] le deuxième cas', with the emphasis 'figure vide existe toujours'. The struck-out phrase 'cela implique que' (not 'signifie') appears to be struck.
